newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt up with U.S. Treasuries, shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt up with U.S. Treasuries, shortcovering.

text.p: A rise in the U.S. Treasury market coupled with shortcovering sent emerging market debt prices higher Thursday, emerging market traders said.

"The market is very strong. We are going through another rally here right now and we are seeing some good volume and good two way flow mostly from buyers," said one emerging markets debt trader from a major U.S. investment bank.
Despite news of a widening trade deficit in Brazil, sources said debt prices still managed to hold gains because much of the news had already been factored into the price.
At 1615 EST/2115 GMT, Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were 3/8 firmer at 70-7/8 bid and the country's par bonds BR4D24=RR were 7/8 stronger at 62-1/8.
"The market had been sell the rumor buy the fact," the first source said, referring to news of Brazil's trade gap of $1.308 billion for October.

"There has been money coming into the market and it looks like some Brazilians that sold paper in the last couple of weeks were coming back covering shorts and buying back bonds so it looks like the street has been able to unload a lot of inventory," he noted.
Meanwhile, sources said growing optimism that the Argentine economy is improving helped to boost its prices.
"Argentina has better propsects after the numbers yesterday," said another trader at a major U.S. firm.
On Wednesday, Argentina announced that its economy grew 6.6 percent in the third quarter compared with the same period last year.
Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR were 5/8 higher at 84-1/2 bid and its par bonds AR4C23=RR were 7/8 stronger at 62-3/8 bid.
Elsewhere, sources said Russia continued to gain support from its Eurobond issue which is now conducting its roadshow.

While one market source said the Eurobond issue did not seem to be getting "great support from the customer base," he noted that the fact it is getting placed is enough good news give Vnesh loans a bounce.
Vneshekonombank dollar-denominated loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were 1/2 stronger at 80-1/2 bid.
Mexico's 2026 global MXUMS=RR were 1/2 firmer at 102-3/4 and Ecuador's pars ECPARS=RR were 1/4 better at 45-3/8.
